reviews.justification: Restricting ongoing unsafe exposure and deciding return to work address different occupational management states and decisions.
The specific hand emergencies could inform triage, but generic triage does not identify one matching decision rule; atomic containment is unestablished.
Pediatric anxiety presentation does not specify separation anxiety or a single diagnostic decision; its apparent breadth cannot establish atomic containment.
Providing culturally sensitive physical support and fulfilling a legal professional duty require different responses despite the shared end-of-life setting.
Interpreting mediastinal or cardiac imaging findings and producing a differential diagnosis are separately scoreable response classes.
Adolescent history taking could involve the confidential interview, but the screening endpoint does not specify confidentiality or its required response.
Both descriptions ask for the diagnostic identification of B12 or folate deficiency macrocytic anemia in the same context; recognition and diagnosis supply no separate target.
Recognizing volvulus as the cause of obstruction differs from recognizing indications for urgent decompression or surgery.
Planning return to work using functional restrictions differs from selecting or applying occupational medical surveillance.
Identifying the obligatory atrial communication is a specific anatomical knowledge response, distinct from diagnosing TAPVR.
Biopsychosocial formulation may inform an integrated intervention plan, but the generic formulation endpoint does not specify whether the required response is the same plan.
Both endpoints describe initial emergency stabilization of acute coronary syndromes with the same action class, stage, and context; no differing management intent is stated.
Identifying precipitating factors is an assessment response, whereas the other endpoint is framed as a management action based on formulation.
Constructing an outpatient safety plan after discharge is judged safe is a subsequent decision to choosing a safe emergency disposition.
Recognition is paired with an action response class without naming the recognized finding or action; shared emergency metadata cannot resolve the intended decision.
Determining contamination for screening and interpreting the hand examination have different required responses; the broader retained reasoning text does not make them identical.
Choosing to obtain collateral history is a data-gathering action, distinct from making a severity-stratified dementia diagnosis.
Determining viability from test results is a specified interpretation response; diagnosing the cause of first-trimester bleeding is a separate diagnostic target.
Recognizing ischemia, perforation, or peritonitis is complication diagnosis, whereas the other endpoint requires an emergency stabilization action.
Absorption factors is an unspecified umbrella with a diagnosis class; it does not establish the same molecular-size prediction or a coherent atomic containing rule.
Documenting care wishes could instantiate an end-of-life professional duty, but the legal endpoint names no duty or matching action.
Selecting a tendon-integrity test is an investigation response; interpreting an examination is a different response class and decision.
The broad legal professional action endpoint does not identify a MAID request or one legal rule, preventing equivalence or atomic containment adjudication.
Generic severe-grief differentiation does not specify comparison with major depression; neither the comparator nor the effect of severity is resolved.
Distinguishing primary from post-infectious lactase deficiency classifies etiology after recognizing the deficiency, a different diagnostic response.
Legally reporting an infection is a distinct duty from the clinical diagnosis or management response named by the other endpoint.
Determining whether diabetes is present and classifying its type are independently scoreable diagnostic decisions.
Recognizing borderline personality disorder and assessing its safety implications concern different knowledge and clinical decisions.
The epidemiology-tagged recognition endpoint never specifies age or racial epidemiology, and its severe-state context and response class leave the intended comparison unresolved.
Research ethical reasoning, even with a consent family tag, does not specify enrolment consent or one rule; broad containment remains unadjudicated.
Diagnosing sigmoid versus cecal volvulus and choosing an emergency stabilization action require different responses.
Classifying orgasmic dysfunction differs from screening for medical, psychiatric, or medication contributors.
The generic investigation interpretation endpoint does not name ECG, laboratory results, or one clinical interpretation rule; a shared response class is insufficient.
First-pass management reasoning does not specify route selection or avoidance of first-pass metabolism, so the exact shared action is unresolved.
Both endpoints target the cardiac differential diagnosis of syncope with the same diagnostic family and context; the recognition wording introduces no distinct response.
Preventing a transporter-mediated interaction and managing first-pass metabolism test different pharmacokinetic mechanisms and actions.
Treating end-of-life pain is a clinical therapeutic action, distinct from a legal professional action.
Obtaining time since injury is a history-gathering response, distinct from making a hand-injury triage diagnosis.
The broad discharge differential does not specify the physiologic-versus-infectious comparison or a single atomic rule.
Explaining pulmonary venous drainage is an anatomical interpretation response, distinct from naming TAPVR as a diagnosis.
Severity-stratified depressive diagnosis may involve a different classification than excluding other psychiatric syndromes; the generic endpoint does not resolve this.
Predicting substrate accumulation from P-glycoprotein inhibition differs in mechanism and response class from a first-pass management action.
Both require identifying the same functional impairment, ulceration, or high-risk location warning features; the family and stage wording does not change that recognition decision.
Assessing access to lethal means gathers one risk factor; deciding whether urgent intervention is required is a separate synthesized risk decision.
Initial ARDS management does not specify resuscitative respiratory support for life-threatening hypoxemia or one atomic management rule.
Cluster recognition across A, B, and C is broader than recognizing cluster C, but the packet does not establish a single atomic containing decision.
Reassessing later functional recovery and interpreting the initial examination before local anesthesia differ in stage and required response.
Both describe diagnostic identification of stenotic or regurgitant valvular lesions in the same context, with no additional decision specified by the differential wording.
Culturally safe care may include advocacy, but the generic care endpoint does not identify action against system barriers or a matching duty.
Providing analgesia is a treatment decision; interpreting nerve function before anesthesia is a separate examination decision.
The generic triage endpoint may concern operative disposition, but its diagnosis class and unspecified triage target do not establish that shared action.
Ensuring valid voluntary consent and counselling that screening is voluntary are related but independently scoreable legal and communication responses.
Recognizing refractory hypoxemia during monitoring is a complication diagnosis, distinct from selecting initial ARDS treatment.
Counselling about recurrence prevention differs from diagnosing or assessing a severe current urinary infection.
P-glycoprotein reasoning does not specify inhibition, substrate concentration, or a direction of effect; matching terminology cannot establish the same prediction.
Recognition is assigned an emergency action class without an explicit recognized state or treatment, leaving its relationship to emergency management unresolved.
Determining wound contamination and interpreting a systematic hand examination, particularly nerve testing before anesthesia, ask for different responses.
The descriptions overlap in culturally safe care but neither resolves one shared action, and the professional-duty versus management framing could change the response.
Both require recognizing brachial plexus injury; motor and sensory distribution describes an evidence path to that same diagnostic decision.
Eliciting resuscitation wishes is a communication response, distinct from carrying out the unspecified legal professional action.
Screening recommendations could target eligibility, intervals, or test selection; the broad endpoint does not identify the specific test-choice decision.
Ongoing neurologic surveillance is a later monitoring decision, distinct from initial severity-stratified trauma assessment.
Generic system navigation does not specify digital modality selection, and its diagnosis response class conflicts with a clearly stated system action.
End-of-life assessment could refer to several clinical or legal decisions; no capacity rule or corresponding response is identified.
Recognizing neurologic deterioration is a diagnostic triage response, whereas the epidural hematoma endpoint requires an emergency stabilization action.
Hospitalizing severe symptomatic infection differs materially from preventive screening of urinary infection in pregnancy.
Gathering mechanism, contamination, and timing is a history-screening task; interpreting the examination requires a different response.
Initiating continuous safety measures for imminent risk is an immediate intervention distinct from deciding the patient's disposition.
The broad communication endpoint names no matching support decision, while the other bundles emotional, physical, and spiritual support; atomic containment is unresolved.
Distinguishing absence seizures from inattention tests recognition of childhood absence epilepsy; the specified comparator supplies evidence for the same diagnosis.
The recognition endpoint is severe or unstable, while assessment is unspecified; the packet does not establish whether severity changes the diagnostic target.
Normal-versus-pathologic maternal adaptation spans multiple possible findings; it does not identify the edema rule or a verified atomic containing decision.
Both concern return to work, but the preventive endpoint leaves the decision rule unspecified and does not resolve whether it requires the same functional planning action.
Providing culturally sensitive emotional support and performing a legal professional duty require distinct communication and ethical responses.
Connecting a family with autism supports is a system-navigation action after recognition, distinct from screening for the disorder.
Other reporting triggers does not specify retirement-home abuse or one governing duty; shared reporting terminology cannot establish atomic containment.
Providing spiritual support and fulfilling a legal professional duty test distinct communication and ethical actions.
Both require recognizing ARDS; the specified hypoxemia, opacities, and noncardiogenic context are evidence for the same diagnostic answer.
Fulfilling an infection-reporting duty and diagnosing the cause of vaginal discharge are independently scoreable legal and diagnostic decisions.
The generic normal-versus-pathologic adaptation endpoint does not identify the concerning-edema rule or establish one atomic broader decision.
Referring severe pulmonary embolism for thrombolysis assessment is a specific management action, distinct from diagnostic recognition across vascular procedures.
